[b]January 20, 2028: A meeting with the Shah[/b]

Well your honour, burbled Cahit through the folds of his chin fat, The bill passed, PETROX will reply to us no doubt, and the oil fields will begin bubbling up, thus reversing half a century of isolationist oil policy, he wheezed slightly as he sat down in his wheelchair, holding a crystal glass of cognac.

Yes, it is a major win for the economy, and a step, at least in my opinion, in the right direction, replied the shah, rejecting the second glass of cognac which Cahit offered him.

The office of Cahit was a dark looming 18th century space housed in an old palace that had been converted into a government office in 1956, it gave villain vibes, though the shah didnt wish to insult the statesman by telling him this.

Now, I have spoken at length with the heads of the various parties in the chamber, and they generally are cautious to affirm a group of homosexuals, said Cahit.

Is that right? Intoned the shah.

They fear, division, among the populace, and frankly you need the votes to begin the austerity measures later this year, stated Cahit.

The intelligence committee has spoken to me Cahit, replied the shah, turning from the window where he had peered out into the bustling street below, There is word, Rosenmarkke might try to get THEP to be involved, 

Cahit scoffed, The Thýven-Hydronia Economic Pact has not been relevant since the fall of sal-baliz two years ago, and Rosenmarkke is a tinpot dictatorship acting like a democracy, 

This may be true, but, said the Shah.

But nothing, your honour, replied Cahit smacking his lips together, Yzakastan must stand firm against the interests of the global community on Shamat, for instance, the SSP, Shamat Security Pact, it has expressed desire to unite shamat under one flag, that is a bigger threat, 

Hardly, replied the shah, The SSP is not relevant to our interests,

And if they attempt consolidation? Asked Cahit.

Then we do what we do best, we unite the parties and push a referendum to reactivate the caliphate, replied the shah.

The caliphate was dissolved by revolutionary mandate, youd have to get the left in on it, replied Cahit with a frown.

Compromise my good sir, but first we must strengthen our position in the ballot box. The PETROX vote was surprisingly successful, how was it done! Asked the Shah.

The oil lobby is quite good at manipulating the prices at the gas station, by having a few of the governors promise to lower the prices, we managed to secure some win, replied Cahit with a chuckle.

Now I expect a decline in prices, warned the shah, Failure to do so will destabilize our goals, he said.

Of course my shah, I have a meeting with Warren this afternoon, do not worry, laughed Cahit grabbing and patting the hand of the Shah.

Very well then, replied the shah wresting his hand from Cahits meaty grip.
